checks.s: The preamble identifies Vantage as 'Vantage Defense Systems, LLC,' a Delaware limited liability company.
The preamble states Vantage's principal office is at 8200 Dominion Ridge Parkway, Suite 600, McLean, VA 22102.
The preamble identifies Meridian as 'Meridian Cyber Solutions, Inc.,' a Virginia corporation.
The preamble states Meridian's principal office is at 1455 Sentry Commons Drive, Suite 310, Reston, VA 20190.
The agreement includes Vantage's CAGE code 7V2K8 in the recitals or a relevant exhibit.
The agreement includes Meridian's CAGE code 3M9F1 in the recitals or a relevant exhibit.
The agreement includes Vantage's UEI number J4M7RKL2XNB3 in the recitals or a relevant exhibit.
The agreement includes Meridian's UEI number R8P3TWY6QAD5 in the recitals or a relevant exhibit.
The Identification of Procurement section references RFP No. HC1028-25-R-0042.
The agreement identifies the program as the Sentinel Shield Enterprise Cybersecurity Program.
The agreement identifies the issuing agency as DISA (Defense Information Systems Agency).
The agreement identifies the anticipated contract type as Cost-Plus-Fixed-Fee (CPFF) with an IDIQ task-order structure.
The agreement states the estimated total contract value is $215,000,000.
The Roles and Responsibilities article designates Vantage as Prime Contractor / Team Lead.
The Roles and Responsibilities article designates Meridian as Subcontractor / Teammate.
The agreement notes Meridian's small-business status under NAICS 541512 with an SBA $34M revenue threshold.
The agreement notes Vantage's other-than-small business status.
The Workshare and Revenue Allocation article or Exhibit A reflects Vantage at 62% ($133,300,000) of the $215M estimated TCV.
The Workshare and Revenue Allocation article or Exhibit A reflects Meridian at 38% ($81,700,000) of the $215M estimated TCV.
The workshare or revenue allocation covers the 5-year base period.
The workshare or revenue allocation covers three 1-year option periods.
The agreement states a target fixed-fee rate of 7.5% on estimated costs.
The financial provisions or Exhibit A reference Meridian's estimated cost base of approximately $76,000,000.
The financial provisions or Exhibit A reference Meridian's estimated fee of approximately $5,700,000.
The Exclusivity and Non-Compete article limits exclusivity to solicitation HC1028-25-R-0042 only.
The Exclusivity and Non-Compete article provides that, if no award is made, exclusivity terminates 12 months after proposal submission (June 20, 2026 or an equivalent description).
The Exclusivity and Non-Compete article provides that exclusivity terminates 60 days after formal agency cancellation of the solicitation.
The B&P Cost Sharing article or Exhibit B states total estimated B&P costs of $1,800,000.
The agreement states Vantage's B&P share is 65% ($1,170,000).
The agreement states Meridian's B&P share is 35% ($630,000).
The agreement states that each party's B&P costs are non-refundable regardless of outcome.
The IP article preserves each party's sole ownership of its background or pre-existing IP.
The IP article grants a non-exclusive, royalty-free license to background or pre-existing IP limited to proposal preparation and contract performance.
The IP article assigns foreground IP to the party that develops it.
The IP article grants the other party a cross-license to foreground IP solely for Government contract performance.
The IP article references DFARS 252.227-7014 (Rights in Other Than Commercial Computer Software and Other Than Commercial Computer Software Documentation) for Government rights.
The IP article references DFARS 252.227-7018 (Rights in Other Than Commercial Technical Data and Computer Software — Small Business Innovation Research (SBIR) Program) for Government rights.
The OCI Mitigation article or Exhibit D discloses Meridian's existing DISA SETI-II Task Order D4017.
The disclosure states that SETI-II Task Order D4017 has a value of $6,200,000.
The disclosure states that SETI-II Task Order D4017 has a PoP through December 31, 2025.
The disclosure states that SETI-II Task Order D4017 performs advisory cybersecurity assessments for the same DISA program office.
The agreement requires Meridian to establish a firewall segregating SETI-II advisory personnel from Sentinel Shield teams.
The agreement states that Meridian will not seek an extension of SETI-II Task Order D4017.
The agreement identifies BridgePoint Consulting Group, LLC as the independent OCI mitigation auditor.
The Insurance Requirements article or Exhibit C specifies Meridian CGL at $2,000,000 per occurrence.
The Insurance Requirements article or Exhibit C specifies Meridian CGL at $5,000,000 aggregate.
The agreement specifies Meridian Professional Liability (E&O) at $10,000,000 per claim.
The agreement specifies Meridian Professional Liability (E&O) at $10,000,000 aggregate.
The agreement specifies Meridian Cyber Liability at $5,000,000.
The agreement specifies Vantage CGL at $5,000,000 per occurrence.
The agreement specifies Vantage CGL at $10,000,000 aggregate.
The agreement specifies Vantage Professional Liability (E&O) at $10,000,000.
The agreement specifies Vantage Cyber Liability at $10,000,000.
The Indemnification article caps Meridian's indemnification to Vantage at the lesser of $81,700,000 (Meridian's workshare value) or 1× aggregate subcontract value invoiced to date.
The Indemnification article caps Vantage's indemnification to Meridian at 1× aggregate payments made to Meridian to date.
The agreement carves IP infringement out from the indemnification caps and makes it uncapped.
The agreement carves willful misconduct out from the indemnification caps and makes it uncapped.
The Termination article allows either party to terminate for convenience before award upon 30 days' written notice if no Government contract has been awarded.
The Termination article allows post-award termination for cause upon material breach with a 30-day cure period.
The Termination article permits immediate termination if the material breach is not cured within the 30-day cure period.
The agreement permits either party to terminate if the other undergoes a >50% ownership transfer without prior written consent.
The Dispute Resolution article requires mandatory senior-executive negotiation for 30 calendar days as a condition precedent to arbitration.
The agreement specifies binding arbitration under AAA Commercial Arbitration Rules.
The agreement specifies Fairfax County, Virginia, as the arbitration venue.
The agreement specifies a panel of 3 arbitrators.
The Governing Law provision specifies the Commonwealth of Virginia without regard to conflicts-of-law principles.
The Notices provision lists Vantage's address as 8200 Dominion Ridge Parkway, Suite 600, McLean, VA 22102.
The Notices provision lists Vantage's attention line as Attn: Col. (Ret.) Dennis W. Hargrove, VP, Contracts.
The Notices provision lists Meridian's address as 1455 Sentry Commons Drive, Suite 310, Reston, VA 20190.
The Notices provision lists Meridian's attention line as Attn: Rachel S. Feinberg, Director of Contracts.
The agreement references the RFP release date of March 14, 2025.
The agreement references the proposal due date of June 20, 2025.
The agreement references the anticipated award date of October 1, 2025.
The agreement states the base period is October 1, 2025 through September 30, 2030.
The agreement states the option period end date is September 30, 2033.

The Post-Award Subcontract Obligations article states Vantage's obligation to negotiate in good faith a definitive subcontract with Meridian consistent with the workshare, revenue allocation, and other terms of the Teaming Agreement.
The Post-Award Subcontract Obligations article references Exhibit E (Form of Subcontract Term Sheet).
The agreement includes Exhibit E (Form of Subcontract Term Sheet).
The Post-Award Subcontract Obligations article or a standalone flow-down section includes FAR/DFARS flow-down provisions referencing DFARS 252.227-7014 and DFARS 252.227-7018.
The Vantage signature block names Garrett P. Landon as the authorized representative.
The Vantage signature block gives Garrett P. Landon's title as SVP, Strategic Captures.
The Meridian signature block names Dr. Priya N. Chakravarti as the authorized representative.
The Meridian signature block gives Dr. Priya N. Chakravarti's title as Chief Growth Officer.
The agreement references the target execution date of April 11, 2025, in the preamble, effective date line, or signature block.

No unresolved template fill-ins remain: blank fill-in lines and unselected parenthetical option-pickers have been replaced with deal-specific information or accompanied by a drafting note explaining what is needed.
The agreement includes a Confidentiality and Non-Disclosure article protecting proprietary and competition-sensitive information.
The Confidentiality and Non-Disclosure article restricts disclosure to personnel with a need to know.
The General Provisions include a provision prohibiting assignment without consent.
The General Provisions include a severability provision.
The General Provisions include an entire agreement provision.
The General Provisions require amendments to be in writing.
The General Provisions include a counterparts provision.
Exhibit A (Workshare Matrix) reflects functional workshare by capability area for SOC operations, threat intelligence, network resilience engineering, and program management.
Exhibit A's percentages and dollar allocations total to the 62%/38% split.
Exhibit C includes a carrier rating requirement of A.M. Best A- VII or better.
Exhibit C includes additional-insured obligations.
Exhibit C includes waiver-of-subrogation obligations.
Exhibit C includes certificate-of-insurance delivery timelines as specified in the insurance requirements summary.
The agreement states three separate 1-year option periods, not a single 3-year option.
The agreement states a maximum total period of 8 years ending September 30, 2033.
Exhibit D (OCI Mitigation Plan) identifies BridgePoint Consulting Group, LLC as the independent auditor who will verify compliance with the firewall and personnel-segregation measures.
Exhibit D includes Meridian's commitment not to seek an extension of SETI-II Task Order D4017 beyond its December 31, 2025 expiration.
